newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases vs dlr on corporate demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases vs dlr on corporate demand.

text.p: Sustained dollar-buying interest from corporate importers on Friday caused the Kenyan shilling to ease further against the dollar in a generally very quiet market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.28 against the dollar from 55.27, while on the pound the shilling was posted at 91.46 from 91.45.
Dealers said the demand was from the oil sector buying at 55.25/30 levels.
"The demand from the oil sector helped buoy the dollar, giving it a short-term relief," one dealer said.
But another dealer said the demand was not enough to move the market because the volumes being traded were very low.
Some dealers expected the shilling to maintain it's firm tone against the dollar as they saw the renewed demand for dollars was short term.
"Demand is not forthcoming and inflows from tea exporters, however small, are still coming in," one dealer said.

The money market was a bit tight. Dealers said the central bank's weekly treasury bill auction seemed to have attracted the funds available in the money market. Overnight rates were remained at 18 percent levels.
